newsitem.title: UK: Gold fixes just easier as German spat continues.
newsitem.headline: Gold fixes just easier as German spat continues.

text.p: The gold market held above its previous resistance at $345.00 per ounce on Friday afternoon as German financial officials exchanged views on the Bundesbank-Bonn differences on revaluing the country's gold reserves.
Dealers said profit taking also took the top off the silver price which had rallied a few cents overnight after spending the rest of the week ignored in the shadow of platinum and palladium.
Gold fixed at $345.60 down 15 cents from the morning fix. New York's August contract was unchanged at $348.60.
Dealers said the producer selling had been hanging over the market. "It's going to be a battle for every dollar on the upside," one dealer said.
Just after the fixing, officials of the Bundesbank and of the German government had further public exchanges revaluation of the country's gold reserves.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said the bank was deeply opposed to the plan which would constrain its activities in the run up to EMU.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan would mean gold being revalued at the market price with a 40 percent discount, he said. Waigel said the plan was not an attack on the Bundesbank.
All the other major European economies have their gold reserves valued in some relationship to the gold market and update the valuation figure on a regular basis.
The Netherlands, for example, revalues every three years to an average of the last three years' fixing minus 30 percent.
Italy revalues quarterly at the average of the last two or six months fixings whichever is the lower.

Silver's brief forage higher overnight ended abruptly after a flurry of trade buying in New York was followed by profit taking. It was valued at $4.76/$4.78 down a cent after failing to pass the $4.85 resistance earlier.
Borrowing late on Thursday pushed the one-month silver lease rate out from about 1.5 percent to around five percent today.
Some dealers said the move in silver was linked to the froth coming off platinum and palladium where market tightness led to abnormally high lease rates and volatile prices.

Dealers said they were backing off palladium after it slumped $20 from its peak on the futures yesterday of $210.20. It was indicated at $178.00/$181.00 and platinum was at $403.50/$407.50, down $10.50 and $5.50 respectively.
